context.objective: Document how this process works, including controls and what remains unresolved.

turns.text: This is our quarterly financial statement preparation and tie-out. We can start when the trial balance, lead sheets, general ledger and FA-13 workbook are available. Q1 to Q3 are usually unaudited and Q4 usually includes audited footnotes.
Talk me through how you turn those available files into the quarterly financial statements and tie them out.

The Fund Accountant rolls forward the approved prior package, ties lead sheets exactly to the trial balance, clears the Excel check sheet and updates Word. We mark an internal tie-out PDF, compare blacklines and retain it in the binder. After Controller, Director and client review, only the clean client-approved PDF and workpapers go to Box, and we notify the client.
What does the Excel check sheet test before you consider it cleared?

Every supported lead-sheet account must agree exactly to the TB and every displayed statement amount must trace to a tied source. The preparer checks footing and cross-references and resolves check-sheet mismatches, including hidden rows, stale links or bad mappings. There is no established materiality tolerance. The client deadline and formal internal approver are both unconfirmed.
When the Controller or Director finds a discrepancy, what happens before the package is sent back for another review?

The Controller returns unresolved differences or presentation issues to the Fund Accountant for correction. We resolve them against the source, rerun the affected checks and retain review evidence before finalization. The Director does final internal review; the client gives final external approval. Marked and blackline copies stay internal; the Box upload uses the clean PDF and workpapers.
What does the blackline comparison check for, and what would make you resolve a difference?

Word Compare is run against prior-quarter and prior year-end statements and an approved comparable fund when appropriate. We explain or correct unexpected changes to amounts, presentation, disclosures and formatting. An unapproved comparator can introduce unsupported disclosures. The records do not confirm the approved checklist or the exact Box path across clients.
If the client requests changes or does not approve the package, what happens to the statements before they can be finalized?

The approval remains outstanding. We correct amounts or presentation, repeat the affected checks and reviews, and obtain client approval before releasing the clean PDF. Unresolved differences block finalization and filing in FA-15A. FA-13 supplies the workbook and FA-15A gets the marked internal evidence. There is no universal contractual deadline in the record.
What most often causes this package to be delayed or sent back, if anything?
